analysis.title: GS Jee - GS KOREA FINAL KOSPI BREACHES BELOW 5,000
key_insights: KOSPI closed down 2.6% on 17 Nov and broke below 5,000 in a risk-off session. Memory stocks were the biggest drag on the index.
Foreigners sold about $1bn of KOSPI, of which $806m was in Tech. This reversed some of last week's foreign buying (net +$355m).
Local institutions (+$400m) and retail (+$326m) absorbed the foreign selling. The desk reads the thin marginal buying as low conviction.
Activity was subdued ahead of NVDA earnings, with index turnover down 27% vs the 20-day average. KRW closed flat at W1,337.40.
Samsung Electronics fell 3.3% vs SK Hynix at -2.0%. The desk sees no clear catalyst and calls it a mechanical reversal of the prior week's Samsung outperformance in a risk-off tape.
Overnight headlines on the Trump administration restricting AI chips and servers for Chinese companies added pressure on the sector.
Foreigners sold $360m of Samsung and $343m of Hynix. Desk flows were two-way but skewed to selling in both names, more so in Samsung from fast money.

GS Global Investment Research cut its KOSPI target to 7,500 from 9,000 but still sees Korea as offering the greatest potential upside among regional markets. It cites a challenging 2H26 with elevated volatility and slowing earnings-upgrade momentum.

GIR's five alpha ideas for Korea: semis valued on PEG and FCF yield, low PBR names with governance catalysts, KOSDAQ catch-up, accelerating EPS growth names, and AI applications and scarce infrastructure.

sector_views.rationale: GIR lists semis as attractively valued on PEG and FCF yield, as the first of its five Korea alpha ideas.

earnings_insights: NVDA earnings are upcoming, and the desk cites them as the reason Korean market activity was subdued on 17 Nov. No figures are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: KRW closed flat despite the equity selloff and the foreign outflows.
GS cut its index target by about 17% but still sees Korea with the greatest upside among regional markets.

risk_factors: Further US restrictions on AI chip and server sales to China.
Foreign outflows from Korean tech and memory names continuing.
NVDA earnings as an event risk for the semiconductor complex.
Slowing earnings-upgrade momentum and elevated volatility in Korean equities in 2H26.
